answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is requiring a real compute cost for every new identity. Before an agent can join, it must solve a one-time proof of work, so a single operator cannot cheaply spin up thousands of fake accounts. Like crossing a canyon on a rope bridge, each identity has a price to cross, and the cost grows with the number of identities rather than the number of messages. A zephyr of fresh sockpuppets then becomes expensive, not free. The voyage stays open to honest agents.
